sanskrit: putraśokābhisaṃtaptaṃ rājānaṃ śokavihvalam viṣaṇṇavadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā vipro vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing the king scorched by grief for his son, overwhelmed by sorrow, his face downcast, the brāhmaṇa spoke these words.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu khalv asi mūḍhas tvaṃ śocyaḥ kim anuśocasi yadā tvām api śocantaḥ śocyā yāsyanti tāṃ gatim
english: Why are you so deluded? You yourself are a thing to be grieved for—why do you grieve? For those who mourn you, themselves to be mourned, will pass to that same destination.

sanskrit: tvaṃ caivāhaṃ ca ye cānye tvāṃ rājan paryupāsate sarve tatra gamiṣyāmo yata evāgatā vayam
english: You and I, O king, and all the others who attend upon you—all of us shall go there, to the very place from which we came.

sanskrit: senajid uvāca kā buddhiḥ kiṃ tapo vipra kaḥ samādhis tapodhana kiṃ jñānaṃ kiṃ śrutaṃ vā te yat prāpya na viṣīdasi
english: Senajit said: What is your wisdom, O brāhmaṇa, what is your austerity, what your contemplation, O you whose wealth is penance? What knowledge, what scripture have you attained, that you do not despair?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca paśya bhūtāni duḥkhena vyatiṣaktāni sarvaśaḥ ātmāpi cāyaṃ na mama sarvā vā pṛthivī mama
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Behold all beings, bound up with suffering on every side. This self even is not mine—or else the whole earth is mine.

sanskrit: yathā mama tathānyeṣām iti buddhyā na me vyathā etāṃ buddhim ahaṃ prāpya na prahṛṣye na ca vyathe
english: "As it is mine, so it is others'"—with this understanding I feel no anguish. Having attained this insight, I neither rejoice nor grieve.

sanskrit: yathā kāṣṭhaṃ ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca sameyātāṃ mahodadhau sametya ca vyapeyātāṃ tadvad bhūtasamāgamaḥ
english: As two logs of driftwood come together upon the great ocean, and having met, drift apart again—just so is the meeting of beings.

sanskrit: evaṃ putrāś ca pautrāś ca jñātayo bāndhavās tathā teṣu sneho na kartavyo viprayogo hi tair dhruvam
english: So it is with sons and grandsons, with kinsmen and relations: no attachment should be formed toward them, for separation from them is certain.

sanskrit: adarśanād āpatitaḥ punaś cādarśanaṃ gataḥ na tvāsau veda na tvaṃ taṃ kaḥ san kam anuśocasi
english: From the unseen he came forth, and to the unseen he has returned again. He does not know you, nor do you know him—being who, do you grieve for whom?

sanskrit: tṛṣṇārtiprabhavaṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkhārtiprabhavaṃ sukham sukhāt saṃjāyate duḥkham evam etat punaḥ punaḥ sukhasyānantaraṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkhasyānantaraṃ sukham
english: Suffering springs from the torment of craving; pleasure springs from the torment of suffering. From pleasure is suffering born again and again; suffering follows hard upon pleasure, and pleasure hard upon suffering.

sanskrit: sukhāt tvaṃ duḥkham āpannaḥ punar āpatsyase sukham na nityaṃ labhate duḥkhaṃ na nityaṃ labhate sukham
english: From pleasure you have fallen into suffering; again you will come upon pleasure. None attains suffering forever, nor does any attain pleasure forever.

sanskrit: nālaṃ sukhāya suhṛdo nālaṃ duḥkhāya śatravaḥ na ca prajñālam arthānāṃ na sukhānām alaṃ dhanam
english: Friends do not suffice for happiness, nor do enemies suffice for sorrow; wisdom does not suffice to win wealth, nor does wealth suffice for happiness.

sanskrit: na buddhir dhanalābhāya na jāḍyam asamṛddhaye lokaparyāyavṛttāntaṃ prājño jānāti netaraḥ
english: Intelligence does not secure the gaining of wealth, nor does dullness ensure poverty. The wise man alone knows the turning course of the world's affairs—not the other.

sanskrit: buddhimantaṃ ca mūḍhaṃ ca śūraṃ bhīruṃ jaḍaṃ kavim durbalaṃ balavantaṃ ca bhāginaṃ bhajate sukham
english: The wise and the foolish, the brave and the timid, the dull and the learned, the weak and the strong—happiness attends upon whoever is destined for it.

sanskrit: dhenur vatsasya gopasya svāminas taskarasya ca payaḥ pibati yas tasyā dhenus tasyeti niścayaḥ
english: A milk-cow may belong to its calf, to the herdsman, to the owner, or to a thief; but the certainty is this: the cow belongs to whoever drinks her milk.

sanskrit: ye ca mūḍhatamā loke ye ca buddheḥ paraṃ gatāḥ te narāḥ sukham edhante kliśyaty antarito janaḥ
english: Those who are most deluded in the world, and those who have passed beyond intellect—these men prosper in happiness; it is the people in between who suffer.

sanskrit: antyeṣu remire dhīrā na te madhyeṣu remire antyaprāptiṃ sukhām āhur duḥkham antaram antayoḥ
english: The steadfast take their delight in the extremes; they do not delight in the middle states. They call the attainment of an extreme a happy thing, and the region between the two extremes a misery.

sanskrit: ye tu buddhisukhaṃ prāptā dvaṃdvātītā vimatsarāḥ tān naivārthā na cānarthā vyathayanti kadā cana
english: But those who have attained the happiness of wisdom, who have passed beyond the dualities and are free of envy—neither gains nor losses ever trouble them.

sanskrit: atha ye buddhim aprāptā vyatikrāntāś ca mūḍhatām te 'tivelaṃ prahṛṣyanti saṃtāpam upayānti ca
english: But those who have not attained wisdom, yet have passed beyond utter folly—they rejoice beyond all measure, and likewise fall into anguish.

sanskrit: nityapramuditā mūḍhā divi devagaṇā iva avalepena mahatā paridṛbdhā vicetasaḥ
english: The deluded are ever exultant, like the hosts of gods in heaven, swollen with great conceit and bereft of understanding.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ duḥkhāntam ālasyaṃ duḥkhaṃ dākṣyaṃ sukhodayam bhūtiś caiva śriyā sārdhaṃ dakṣe vasati nālase
english: Idleness is a pleasure that ends in pain; diligence is a pain whose outcome is pleasure. Prosperity, together with fortune, dwells in the diligent man and not in the slothful.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ dveṣyaṃ vā yadi vā priyam prāptaṃ prāptam upāsīta hṛdayenāparājitaḥ
english: Whether it be pleasure or pain, the hateful or the dear, let a man meet each thing as it comes, with a heart that is never overcome.

sanskrit: śokasthānasahasrāṇi harṣasthānaśatāni ca divase divase mūḍham āviśanti na paṇḍitam
english: Thousands of occasions for grief and hundreds of occasions for joy assail the fool day after day, but not the wise man.

sanskrit: buddhimantaṃ kṛtaprajñaṃ śuśrūṣum anasūyakam dāntaṃ jitendriyaṃ cāpi śoko na spṛśate naram
english: Sorrow does not touch the man who is wise, of ripened understanding, eager to learn and free of malice, self-controlled and master of his senses.

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhiṃ samāsthāya guptacittaś cared budhaḥ udayāstamayajñaṃ hi na śokaḥ spraṣṭum arhati
english: Holding fast to this understanding, with a guarded mind let the wise man go his way; for sorrow has no right to touch one who knows the rising and the setting of all things.

sanskrit: yannimittaṃ bhavec chokas trāso vā duḥkham eva vā āyāso vā yatomūlas tad ekāṅgam api tyajet
english: Whatever is the cause of grief, of terror, of pain itself, or of toil—from whatever root these spring, let a man renounce it, though it be a very limb of himself.

sanskrit: yad yat tyajati kāmānāṃ tat sukhasyābhipūryate kāmānusārī puruṣaḥ kāmān anu vinaśyati
english: Whatever of his desires a man renounces, by just so much is he filled with happiness. The man who runs after his desires perishes in the wake of those desires.

sanskrit: yac ca kāmasukhaṃ loke yac ca divyaṃ mahat sukham tṛṣṇākṣayasukhasyaite nārhataḥ ṣoḍaśīṃ kalām
english: Whatever pleasure of desire there is in this world, and whatever great pleasure there is in heaven—these are not worth a sixteenth part of the happiness that comes from the extinction of craving.

sanskrit: pūrvadehakṛtaṃ karma śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham prājñaṃ mūḍhaṃ tathā śūraṃ bhajate yādṛśaṃ kṛtam
english: The deed done in a former body, whether good or evil, attends upon the wise man, the fool, and the brave alike, according to the nature of what was done.

sanskrit: evam eva kilaitāni priyāṇy evāpriyāṇi ca jīveṣu parivartante duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca
english: Even so do these things—the dear and the unwelcome, the sorrows and the joys—revolve and recur among living beings.

sanskrit: tad evaṃ buddhim āsthāya sukhaṃ jīved guṇānvitaḥ sarvān kāmāñ jugupseta saṅgān kurvīta pṛṣṭhataḥ vṛtta eṣa hṛdi prauḍho mṛtyur eṣa manomayaḥ
english: Therefore, taking his stand on this understanding, let the man of virtue live in happiness. Let him shun all desires and put attachments behind him; for this swelling tide within the heart is Death himself, fashioned of the mind.

sanskrit: yadā saṃharate kāmān kūrmo 'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ tadātmajyotir ātmā ca ātmany eva prasīdati
english: When a man draws in his desires from every side, as a tortoise draws in its limbs, then the self, become its own light, finds peace within the self alone.

sanskrit: kiṃ cid eva mamatvena yadā bhavati kalpitam tad eva paritāpārthaṃ sarvaṃ saṃpadyate tadā
english: Whenever anything at all is appropriated with the thought "this is mine," that very thing then becomes, in its entirety, an occasion for torment.

sanskrit: na bibheti yadā cāyaṃ yadā cāsmān na bibhyati yadā necchati na dveṣṭi brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: When a man fears nothing, and nothing fears him, when he neither craves nor hates—then he attains to brahman.

sanskrit: ubhe satyānṛte tyaktvā śokānandau bhayābhaye priyāpriye parityajya praśāntātmā bhaviṣyasi
english: Casting off both truth and falsehood, both sorrow and joy, both fear and fearlessness, and abandoning the dear and the hateful, you shall become a soul wholly at peace.

sanskrit: yadā na kurute dhīraḥ sarvabhūteṣu pāpakam karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: When the steadfast man works no evil toward any living being, in deed, in thought, or in word, then he attains to brahman.

sanskrit: yā dustyajā durmatibhir yā na jīryati jīryataḥ yo 'sau prāṇāntiko rogas tāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham
english: That craving which the foolish-minded find so hard to abandon, which does not age though the body ages, that disease which ends only with life's breath—happy is he who casts it off.

sanskrit: atra piṅgalayā gītā gāthāḥ śrūyanti pārthiva yathā sā kṛcchrakāle 'pi lebhe dharmaṃ sanātanam
english: On this matter, O king, are heard the verses sung by Piṅgalā, telling how she, even in her hour of distress, attained the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: saṃkete piṅgalā veśyā kāntenāsīd vinākṛtā atha kṛcchragatā śāntāṃ buddhim āsthāpayat tadā
english: At the appointed trysting-place the courtesan Piṅgalā was left bereft by her lover; then, fallen into distress, she fixed her mind upon a serene resolve.

sanskrit: piṅgalovāca unmattāham anunmattaṃ kāntam anvavasaṃ ciram antike ramaṇaṃ santaṃ nainam adhyagamaṃ purā
english: Piṅgalā said: I, a madwoman, long pursued a lover who was no madman. Though my true beloved was near at hand, until now I never found him.

sanskrit: ekasthūṇaṃ navadvāram apidhāsyāmy agārakam kā hi kāntam ihāyāntam ayaṃ kānteti maṃsyate
english: This little house with its single pillar and nine doors I shall now bolt shut. What woman, when a lover comes to her, would still think, "this is my beloved"?

sanskrit: akāmāḥ kāmarūpeṇa dhūrtā narakarūpiṇaḥ na punar vañcayiṣyanti pratibuddhāsmi jāgṛmi
english: Loveless rogues in the guise of lovers, hell-shaped deceivers—they shall cheat me no more. I am awakened now; I am awake.

sanskrit: anartho 'pi bhavaty artho daivāt pūrvakṛtena vā saṃbuddhāhaṃ nirākārā nāham adyājitendriyā
english: Even calamity becomes a blessing, by fate or by deeds done before. I am awakened, free of all longing; no longer am I one whose senses are unmastered.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ nirāśaḥ svapiti nairāśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham āśām anāśāṃ kṛtvā hi sukhaṃ svapiti piṅgalā
english: He who is without hope sleeps in peace; hopelessness is the highest happiness. Having turned hope into the absence of hope, Piṅgalā sleeps in peace.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etaiś cānyaiś ca viprasya hetumadbhiḥ prabhāṣitaiḥ paryavasthāpito rājā senajin mumude sukham
english: Bhīṣma said: By these and other reasoned utterances of the brāhmaṇa King Senajit was set firmly at rest, and he rejoiced in happiness.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca atikrāmati kāle 'smin sarvabhūtakṣayāvahe kiṃ śreyaḥ pratipadyeta tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: As this time slips away, bringing destruction to all beings, what good should a man pursue? Tell me that, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam pituḥ putreṇa saṃvādaṃ tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale, a dialogue of a son with his father. Mark it well, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: dvijāteḥ kasya cit pārtha svādhyāyaniratasya vai babhūva putro medhāvī medhāvī nāma nāmataḥ
english: To a certain brāhmaṇa, O Pārtha, who was devoted to the recitation of the Veda, there was born a son of keen mind, Medhāvin by name.

sanskrit: so 'bravīt pitaraṃ putraḥ svādhyāyakaraṇe ratam mokṣadharmārthakuśalo lokatattvavicakṣaṇaḥ
english: That son, skilled in the meaning of the dharma of liberation and discerning in the true nature of the world, spoke to his father, who was absorbed in the recitation of the Veda.

sanskrit: dhīraḥ kiṃ svit tāta kuryāt prajānan; kṣipraṃ hy āyur bhraśyate mānavānām pitas tad ācakṣva yathārthayogaṃ; mamānupūrvyā yena dharmaṃ careyam
english: What should a steadfast and discerning man do, dear father, seeing that the lifespan of men slips swiftly away? Tell me this in accord with the truth, father, so that, in due order, I may practise the dharma.

sanskrit: pitovāca vedān adhītya brahmacaryeṇa putra; putrān icchet pāvanārthaṃ pitṝṇām agnīn ādhāya vidhivac ceṣṭayajño; vanaṃ praviśyātha munir bubhūṣet
english: The father said: Having studied the Vedas in chastity, my son, let a man desire sons for the purifying of his ancestors; then, having duly established the sacred fires and offered sacrifice, let him enter the forest and seek to become a sage.

sanskrit: putra uvāca evam abhyāhate loke samantāt parivārite amoghāsu patantīṣu kiṃ dhīra iva bhāṣase
english: The son said: When the world is thus stricken and beset on every side, when the unerring shafts are falling, how can you speak as though you were a man of calm wisdom?

sanskrit: pitovāca katham abhyāhato lokaḥ kena vā parivāritaḥ amoghāḥ kāḥ patantīha kiṃ nu bhīṣayasīva mām
english: The father said: How is the world stricken? By what is it beset? What unerring shafts are falling here? Why do you seek, as it were, to frighten me?

sanskrit: putra uvāca mṛtyunābhyāhato loko jarayā parivāritaḥ ahorātrāḥ patanty ete nanu kasmān na budhyase
english: The son said: The world is stricken by death and beset by old age; these days and nights are the falling shafts. How is it you do not understand?

sanskrit: yadāham etaj jānāmi na mṛtyus tiṣṭhatīti ha so 'haṃ kathaṃ pratīkṣiṣye jālenāpihitaś caran
english: When I know this—that death never stands still—how, then, shall I wait, moving about as I am with the net cast over me?

sanskrit: rātryāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyām āyur alpataraṃ yadā gādhodake matsya iva sukhaṃ vindeta kas tadā tad eva vandhyaṃ divasam iti vidyād vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: When with every passing night the span of life grows ever shorter, who could find any joy, like a fish in shallowing water? Let the discerning man know that very day to be barren and lost.

sanskrit: anavāpteṣu kāmeṣu mṛtyur abhyeti mānavam śaṣpāṇīva vicinvantam anyatragatamānasam vṛkīvoraṇam āsādya mṛtyur ādāya gacchati
english: While his desires are yet unfulfilled, death comes upon a man as he gathers his pleasures like tender shoots, his mind set elsewhere; like a she-wolf seizing a lamb, death takes him and departs.

sanskrit: adyaiva kuru yac chreyo mā tvā kālo 'tyagād ayam akṛteṣv eva kāryeṣu mṛtyur vai saṃprakarṣati
english: This very day do what is good; let not this moment slip past you. For while one's tasks are still undone, death drags a man away.

sanskrit: śvaḥkāryam adya kurvīta pūrvāhṇe cāparāhṇikam na hi pratīkṣate mṛtyuḥ kṛtaṃ vāsya na vā kṛtam ko hi jānāti kasyādya mṛtyusenā nivekṣyate
english: Let a man do tomorrow's task today, and the afternoon's work in the morning; for death does not wait to ask whether one's work is done or undone. Who knows upon whom the army of death will descend this very day?

sanskrit: yuvaiva dharmaśīlaḥ syād animittaṃ hi jīvitam kṛte dharme bhavet kīrtir iha pretya ca vai sukham
english: While still young let a man be devoted to dharma, for life is uncertain and without warning. When dharma is practised, there is renown here and, after death, happiness as well.

sanskrit: mohena hi samāviṣṭaḥ putradārārtham udyataḥ kṛtvā kāryam akāryaṃ vā puṣṭim eṣāṃ prayacchati
english: For a man possessed by delusion, toiling for the sake of wife and children, doing what ought and what ought not to be done, devotes himself to their nourishment.

sanskrit: taṃ putrapaśusaṃmattaṃ vyāsaktamanasaṃ naram suptaṃ vyāghraṃ mahaugho vā mṛtyur ādāya gacchati
english: That man, intoxicated with sons and cattle, his mind ensnared—death takes him and departs, as a great flood carries off a sleeping tiger.

sanskrit: saṃcinvānakam evaikaṃ kāmānām avitṛptakam vyāghraḥ paśum ivādāya mṛtyur ādāya gacchati
english: While he is still heaping up the objects of his desire, unsated, all alone, death takes him and departs, as a tiger seizes its prey.

sanskrit: idaṃ kṛtam idaṃ kāryam idam anyat kṛtākṛtam evam īhāsukhāsaktaṃ kṛtāntaḥ kurute vaśe
english: "This is done, this remains to be done, this other thing is half-finished"—the man so caught up in the pleasure of striving, fate brings under its sway.

sanskrit: kṛtānāṃ phalam aprāptaṃ karmaṇāṃ phalasaṅginam kṣetrāpaṇagṛhāsaktaṃ mṛtyur ādāya gacchati
english: Before he has gained the fruit of deeds already done, while he still clings to that fruit, attached to field and shop and house, death takes him and departs.

sanskrit: mṛtyur jarā ca vyādhiś ca duḥkhaṃ cānekakāraṇam anuṣaktaṃ yadā dehe kiṃ svastha iva tiṣṭhasi
english: Death and old age and disease, and suffering with its many causes, cling fast to the body—why, then, do you stand as though you were safe and at ease?

sanskrit: jātam evāntako 'ntāya jarā cānveti dehinam anuṣaktā dvayenaite bhāvāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ
english: From the very moment of its birth, the destroyer pursues the embodied being toward its end, and old age follows after it. By this pair are all things bound, the moving and the unmoving alike.

sanskrit: mṛtyor vā gṛham evaitad yā grāme vasato ratiḥ devānām eṣa vai goṣṭho yad araṇyam iti śrutiḥ
english: The delight a man takes in dwelling in the village is nothing but the very house of death; the wilderness, says the sacred tradition, is the meeting-ground of the gods.

sanskrit: nibandhanī rajjur eṣā yā grāme vasato ratiḥ chittvaināṃ sukṛto yānti naināṃ chindanti duṣkṛtaḥ
english: The delight a man takes in dwelling in the village is the rope that binds him fast. The doers of good cut it through and go free; the doers of evil do not cut it.

sanskrit: na hiṃsayati yaḥ prāṇān manovākkāyahetubhiḥ jīvitārthāpanayanaiḥ karmabhir na sa badhyate
english: He who does no harm to living creatures by thought, word, or body, nor by deeds that would strip another of life and livelihood—that man is not bound.

sanskrit: na mṛtyusenām āyāntīṃ jātu kaś cit prabādhate ṛte satyam asaṃtyājyaṃ satye hy amṛtam āśritam
english: None can ever turn back the oncoming army of death, save by truth, which must never be forsaken; for in truth the immortal abides.

sanskrit: tasmāt satyavratācāraḥ satyayogaparāyaṇaḥ satyārāmaḥ samo dāntaḥ satyenaivāntakaṃ jayet
english: Therefore let a man, keeping the vow and practice of truth, devoted to the discipline of truth, taking his delight in truth, even-minded and self-controlled, conquer the destroyer by truth alone.

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuś ca dvayaṃ dehe pratiṣṭhitam mṛtyum āpadyate mohāt satyenāpadyate 'mṛtam
english: Both the immortal and death are established within the body. Through delusion one comes upon death; through truth one comes upon the immortal.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ hy ahiṃsraḥ satyārthī kāmakrodhabahiṣkṛtaḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣemī mṛtyuṃ hāsyāmy amartyavat
english: And so I, harmless, seeking truth, having cast out desire and anger, the same in suffering and in pleasure, secure in peace, shall leave death behind me like one who is immortal.

sanskrit: śāntiyajñarato dānto brahmayajñe sthito muniḥ vāṅmanaḥkarmayajñaś ca bhaviṣyāmy udagāyane
english: Delighting in the sacrifice of peace, self-controlled, a sage established in the sacrifice of brahman, performing the sacrifice of word, mind, and deed, I shall become such a one in the northward course of the sun.

sanskrit: paśuyajñaiḥ kathaṃ hiṃsrair mādṛśo yaṣṭum arhati antavadbhir uta prājñaḥ kṣatrayajñaiḥ piśācavat
english: How could a wise man such as I fittingly worship with cruel animal sacrifices, whose fruit is perishable—or, like a flesh-eating demon, with the sacrifices of warriors?

sanskrit: yasya vāṅmanasī syātāṃ samyak praṇihite sadā tapas tyāgaś ca yogaś ca sa vai sarvam avāpnuyāt
english: He whose speech and mind are always rightly composed, who has austerity, renunciation, and yoga—he indeed shall attain everything.

sanskrit: nāsti vidyāsamaṃ cakṣur nāsti vidyāsamaṃ balam nāsti rāgasamaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāsti tyāgasamaṃ sukham
english: There is no eye equal to knowledge; there is no strength equal to knowledge. There is no suffering equal to passion; there is no happiness equal to renunciation.

sanskrit: ātmany evātmanā jāta ātmaniṣṭho 'prajo 'pi vā ātmany eva bhaviṣyāmi na māṃ tārayati prajā
english: Born of the self by the self alone, established in the self, even though I be without offspring, I shall abide in the self alone; no offspring delivers me.

sanskrit: naitādṛśaṃ brāhmaṇasyāsti vittaṃ; yathaikatā samatā satyatā ca śīle sthitir daṇḍanidhānam ārjavaṃ; tatas tataś coparamaḥ kriyābhyaḥ
english: No wealth such as this belongs to a brāhmaṇa—oneness, even-mindedness, and truthfulness, steadfastness in good conduct, the laying down of the rod of violence, uprightness, and, beyond all these, withdrawal from action.
